name: Masters – Colour, Size, UOM
screen: Setup › Colour Card / Size Range / UOM
description: Colour card, size range, UOM master and material-wise UOM conversion that every WFX transaction reads from.
one_line: The shared lists – colours, sizes and units – that every WFX document must pick from.
theory: Masters are the shared vocabulary of WFX. A colour card groups colour codes; a size range groups size codes; the UOM master lists units, and the UOM conversion table says how one unit converts to another for a specific material. Nothing in a transaction can use a colour, size or unit that is not in a master. Styles pick a colour card and size range, and every downstream line (BOM, booking, OC, MRP, FPO) carries the same codes, which is what lets you trace one colour from design to the factory floor.

name: Apparel Style (Techpack)
description: Style Flannel Shirt Adi (NIS-58) header, base colour list and base size list that drive BOM dependencies and order breakups.
one_line: The finished garment: who buys it, which colour card and size range it uses, and how it is purchased and priced.
theory: The style (apparel techpack) is the finished-goods article. It fixes the buyer, department, colour card and size range, and lists which of those colours and sizes the style is offered in (base colour list, base size list). The base lists are the "rows" that the BOM dependency maps from: every style colour must be mapped to a material colour or explicitly left as Not Used.

name: BOM – Materials & Dependency
description: BOM material lines with consumption, wastage, loss and shrinkage maths, price conversion and colour/size dependency.
one_line: How much of each material one garment needs, at what price, and which material colour goes with which garment colour.
theory: The Bill of Materials lists every raw material needed to make one garment. Each line says which material, how much of it per garment (consumption), what allowances are added (wastage, loss, shrinkage), what it costs, and – through dependency – which material colour/size is used for each garment colour/size. Final Consumption is the single most important number on the BOM: MRP multiplies garment quantity by it to get fabric demand, and FPO multiplies factory quantity by it to get fabric to issue. Price is entered per Purchase UOM (what the supplier invoices) and converted to Cons UOM (what the garment consumes) using the material UOM conversion.

name: BOM – Routing
description: Production processes, operations and material linkage of BOM #1 DP, which later become FPPO process orders.
one_line: The ordered processes that make the garment, what each costs (Cost Of × Production Time) and which material each consumes.
theory: Routing is the ordered list of production processes that turn materials into the garment. Each process has an output item, the process it follows, and a rate. Operations break a process into machine-level steps with time. Material linkage tells WFX which process consumes a BOM material – fabric N-8 is required for VCutting. This is why the Level 2 production indent shows "Required For: VCutting".

name: BOM – Costing
description: Material cost, production cost, total cost, profit, profit % and markup % for BOM #1 DP.
one_line: Cost per piece – material plus production – against the selling price: Profit uses the price after discount, Markup the price before it.
theory: Costing rolls up the BOM into a per-piece cost and compares it with the selling price. Material cost comes from BOM line values grouped by section; production cost comes from routing process rates. Profit % = (selling price after discount − total cost) ÷ selling price after discount. Markup % = (selling price before discount − total cost) ÷ total cost. Adi TShirt (NIS-59): −597.66 % and −84.07 %.

name: Raw Material Techpack
description: Fabric article N-8 master: UOMs, colour card, dependency, buying price and cross-document checks.
one_line: The master of a purchasable material – fabric or trim: its units, colour card, pricing basis and how stock is tracked.
theory: The raw-material techpack is the master of a purchasable material. It defines UOMs (consumption, purchase, storage, secondary), the colour card, how the material depends on garment colour/size, and default buying price. Material Dependency = ColorSize means stock and demand are kept per colour and size, which is why the stock key is Article|Colour|Size (e.g. N-8|372|34S).

name: Buyer Block Booking (BBB)
description: Projection booking PPJ179 that reserves fabric by colour and size before a confirmed buyer order exists.
one_line: A projection that lets you book and buy long-lead fabric before the buyer confirms the order.
theory: A Buyer Block Booking (BBB) is a projection: the buyer signals expected volume before confirming styles. It lets sourcing reserve and buy long-lead material (fabric) early, by colour and size. Material bought against the booking is stocked with the booking number. When the confirmed OC arrives and MRP runs, that stock is adjusted in-house automatically, so only the gap is purchased again.

name: BBB Adhoc Indent
description: Manual indent PPM-000735-001 of type Buyer Block Booking: buys the booked fabric before any sales order exists.
one_line: A purchase request raised by hand against the block booking – not by MRP and not for a sales order.
theory: An indent is an internal request to buy material. An adhoc indent is raised manually (not by MRP); here it is raised against booking PPJ179 so the material carries the booking reference. Each indent line can only take up to the booking balance. Once a PO covers the full indent qty the open qty becomes 0 and the indent is Completed.

name: RMPO – Raw Material Purchase Order
description: Purchase orders 1229 (against the adhoc indent) and 1230 (against the MRP production indent) with value and open qty maths.
one_line: The purchase order to the supplier. Value = ordered qty × PO price; open qty closes as GRN accepts material.
theory: The RMPO is the commitment to the supplier. Lines come from indent lines; quantity can be increased by MOQ/MCQ/MSQ rules or additional qty; value is ordered qty × PO price plus surcharge. Two RMPOs exist for Flannel Shirt Adi (NIS-58): 1229 against the adhoc (booking) indent – fully received – and 1230 against the MRP production indent for the 1,100 KG_Nis not covered by booking stock.

name: GRN – Goods Receipt Note
screen: Inventory › GRN (ASN from Supplier – Against PO)
description: Receipt of RMPO 1229 into the cut store: balance, received, rejected, accepted qty and stock keys.
one_line: Receipt of material against a PO. Only accepted qty becomes stock, tagged with the PO's booking.
theory: A Goods Receipt Note records material physically received at a site against a PO. Balance qty limits what can be received; accepted qty (received − rejected) becomes stock with the PO's stock key and booking number. Accepted qty flows back to the RMPO as shipped qty and closes its open qty.

name: Purchase Order from Buyer (OC)
description: Order confirmation GAPS.NEWOC -249 with delivery OC, colour × size quantity breakup and selling value.
one_line: The confirmed buyer order. Its colour × size breakup is the demand MRP plans from.
theory: The buyer purchase order, captured as an Order Confirmation (OC), is the confirmed demand. A main OC holds one or more delivery OCs; each delivery OC has a BOM, a delivery date and a colour × size quantity breakup. Confirming the OC triggers MRP: the breakup becomes Level 1 garment demand and is exploded through the BOM.

name: MRP – Material Requirement Planning
description: MRP run for the OC: Level 1 garment production demand and Level 2 fabric purchase demand from BOM explosion.
one_line: Turns the buyer order into requirements: garment to make (Level 1) and materials to buy (Level 2).
theory: MRP converts confirmed order quantity into requirements level by level. Level 1 is the garment itself (production demand). Level 2 is every BOM material, found by multiplying Level 1 quantity by Final Consumption for the mapped material colour/size (purchase demand). Demand type decides the next document: production demand → production order; purchase demand for fabric/trims → RMPO; purchase demand for a garment should create a GMPO.

name: Sales Order Indents (MRP)
description: Indents MRP raises for the sales order: Manufacture Indent (Level 1, garment) and Production Indent (Level 2, fabric) with in-house adjustment from BBB stock.
one_line: The two indents MRP raises for a sales order: a Manufacture Indent to make the garment and a Production Indent to buy the fabric.
theory: MRP writes its requirements as indents. The Level 1 manufacture indent asks production to make 1,000 garments. The Level 2 production indent asks purchasing for 1,500 KG_Nis of N-8. Before ordering, the production indent adjusts available stock with the same stock key in-house. 400 KG_Nis from booking PPJ179 (100 per colour/size) is reserved, so only 1,100 goes to RMPO 1230.

name: Production Order
description: Production order PPS12SO/11325 and colour-wise style quantities allocated to the factory production order.
one_line: The make order for the sales order; decides colour quantities released to the factory.
theory: A production order represents the Level 1 manufacture demand of an OC. "Add Style Quantities" decides, per colour, how much goes into the factory production order – Qty % can hold some back.

name: FPO & FPPO
description: Factory production order PPS12FP0158, fabric requirement, stock material allocation and process orders per colour and size.
one_line: Releases quantity to a factory, checks fabric against it and creates one process order per routing step.
theory: The Factory Production Order (FPO) releases quantity to a factory. WFX explodes it again through the BOM to get fabric required, then allocates stock: what is already reserved (from booking stock) is "instructed", the rest stays open until RMPO 1230 is received. Each routing process becomes a Factory Production Process Order (FPPO) carrying the full FPO qty per colour/size.
